synthesis.body: If a projection renders into a fresh temp dir and the rendered output is then copied into the working tree, any merge-with-existing semantics in the projecting code (merge-managed-key-only for JSON, preserve-outside-block for managed-block-inline) sees only the empty temp dir — the merge target is always blank — so the working tree's unrelated keys / outside-block content gets clobbered on the copy step. For real-write modes, project DIRECTLY into the working tree so the merge/splice code sees the existing state. For dry-run, clone the relevant subset of the working tree into a shadow temp dir first, project into the clone, then diff clone vs working tree. Bit us in the post-EXECUTE review of RFC-0001's distribution-adapters spec; the unit tests passed because they re-ran into the same output dir (which carried the prior render), but the integrated --self path broke silently.

title: Render-to-temp + copy breaks merge/splice on-conflict against the working tree
